items.title: Rescue operation unfolds as debris in Iran identified as U.S. F-15E

featured_image.name: F-15 squadron that destroyed Iranian drones returns to Middle East

items.description: Images of fighter jet wreckage surfaced on Iranian state media on Friday, April 3, as independent analysts identified the debris as belonging to a U.S. Air Force F-15E Strike Eagle — not the F-35 stealth jet Iran initially claimed to have downed. Geolocated footage from southern Iran simultaneously revealed an American combat search-and-rescue operation underway deep inside Iranian territory, in what could mark the first confirmed loss of a crewed U.S. aircraft over Iran since the start of Operation Epic Fury on February 28.

items.title: Iran claims capture of US pilot after F-15E allegedly downed

featured_image.name: U.S. Denies F-15E Strike Eagle Went Down In Iran - Yahoo

items.description:
Unconfirmed reports emerged on Friday suggesting that the pilot of a U.S. Air Force F-15E Strike Eagle may have been captured by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps after the aircraft was apparently shot down over Iranian territory, marking what would be the first known loss of a crewed American fighter jet over Iran since the start of Operation Epic Fury.

Iranian state media initially claimed on April 3 that IRGC air defenses had destroyed a second U.S. F-35 stealth fighter over central Iran. However, images from the crash site — showing the remains of a vertical stabilizer bearing markings consistent with the 494th Fighter Squadron, part of the 48th Fighter Wing based at RAF Lakenheath in the United Kingdom — indicate the aircraft was an F-15E Strike Eagle, not an F-35.[1][2][3]

items.title: CMA CGM ship becomes first Western European vessel to cross Hormuz since Iran war

featured_image.name: CMA CGM vessel transits Hormuz Strait - Container News

items.description:
A container ship owned by France's CMA CGM has exited the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first known transit by a vessel linked to Western Europe since the war between the United States, Israel, and Iran all but shuttered the vital waterway in late February.[1][2]

The Maltese-flagged CMA CGM Kribi sailed from waters off Dubai on Thursday afternoon local time, broadcasting "owner France" on its transponder system as it navigated a channel between the Iranian islands of Qeshm and Larak, according to Bloomberg. By Friday morning, the vessel signaled it was off Muscat, Oman. The ship is believed to be heading toward Pointe Noire in the Republic of Congo as part of a service linking India, the Middle East Gulf, and Africa.[3][4][2][5]

items.title: Global food prices jump for second straight month as Middle East war disrupts supply chains

featured_image.name: Consumer prices rose 2.4% annually in February, as expected - CNBC

items.description:
Global food commodity prices rose for a second consecutive month in March, climbing 2.4 percent as the escalating conflict in the Middle East sent energy and fertilizer costs surging through agricultural supply chains, according to data released Friday by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations.

The FAO Food Price Index, which tracks monthly changes in a basket of internationally traded food commodities, averaged 128.5 points in March, up from a revised 125.5 in February. The increase marks the sharpest monthly jump in the index since mid-2025 and follows February's 0.9 percent rise, which had ended a five-month streak of declines.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: South Korea, France elevate ties to strategic partnership

featured_image.name: Macron visits Japan and South Korea, both worried about war in Iran

items.description:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and French President Emmanuel Macron elevated their countries' relationship to a "global strategic partnership" on Friday following summit talks in Seoul, marking the most notable overhaul of bilateral ties in more than two decades.[1][2]

The upgrade replaces a "comprehensive partnership for the 21st century" that had been in place since 2004. It comes as the two nations celebrate the 140th anniversary of diplomatic relations and seek closer alignment on defense, energy security, and advanced technology amid what French officials described as "significant international and regional tensions".[2][3][1]
